steps.say: Lupus is the attacker of every organ through immune complexes. Heart, lung, bowel, blood, and eyes each have a signature lesion. This figure is the map of the multisystem territory. Organ flares require organ specific therapy on top of systemic control.
steps.tx: Systemic lupus erythematosus (**SLE**, multisystem immune complex disease) injures organs through deposited complexes with complement. Cardiac, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, haematologic, and ophthalmic lesions each carry a signature pattern below. Every new organ symptom in lupus is active disease until proven otherwise, and requires organ specific therapy over systemic control.

vis.alt: Diagram of multisystem lupus manifestations with autoantibodies and immune complex pathogenesis.
vis.caption: Immune complexes deposit across heart, lung, bowel, blood, and eyes together. Each organ below has its own signature. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Pericarditis is the commonest cardiac lesion at 25 to 50 percent. Positional pleuritic pain with a friction rub is the definition. Libman-Sacks vegetations are sterile and embolic. Coronary risk is multiplied up to 50-fold in young women.
steps.tx: Cardiac disease spans all layers: **pericarditis** (outer sac inflammation) is commonest at **25 to 50 percent** with positional pleuritic chest pain and friction rub. **Libman-Sacks** endocarditis (sterile wart-like valve vegetations) coats mitral and aortic valves, links to antiphospholipid antibodies, and throws cardioembolic strokes. Accelerated **atherosclerosis** (premature arterial plaque) multiplies infarction risk **5 to 10-fold**, above **50-fold** in young premenopausal women.

steps.say: Lung disease in lupus runs from pleurisy to hemorrhage. Diffuse alveolar bleeding with falling haematocrit is the emergency. Shrinking lung restricts volumes without parenchymal disease. Breathlessness with falling blood counts is bled lungs until proven otherwise.
steps.tx: Pulmonary disease spans acute lupus **pneumonitis** (inflammatory lung infiltrates), diffuse alveolar **haemorrhage** (bleeding into air sacs, an emergency with hemoptysis and falling hematocrit), exudative pleural effusions, and chronic fibrosing interstitial disease. **Shrinking lung syndrome** gives progressive dyspnea with raised hemidiaphragms and restrictive volumes but no parenchymal scarring. Falling hematocrit with breathlessness indicates hemorrhage, not infection.

steps.say: Lupus enteritis gives severe acute abdominal pain with vomiting. CT shows thickened bowel with target and comb signs. Ischaemia is the threat without pulse therapy. Surgical abdomens in lupus are vasculitis until proven otherwise.
steps.tx: Lupus mesenteric **vasculitis** (lupus enteritis, bowel vessel inflammation) presents with severe acute abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Abdominal CT shows bowel wall thickening with **target sign** (layered enhancement rings) and engorged mesenteric vessels called the **comb sign**. Ischaemia and perforation threaten without pulse glucocorticoids. An acute abdomen in active lupus indicates enteritis first, with surgical causes excluded in parallel.

steps.say: Blood counts are the trackers of lupus activity over time. Warm autoimmune haemolysis, immune platelet destruction, and lymphopenia below 1000 are the markers of flares. Lymphopenia is the most faithful marker. Falling counts with active serology require escalation.
steps.tx: Haematologic disease includes warm IgG Coombs-positive autoimmune haemolytic **anaemia** (antibody coated red cells), immune **thrombocytopenia** (antibody destroyed platelets), and leukopenia with **lymphopenia** (low lymphocytes). Lymphopenia below **1,000** per microliter tracks active systemic flares most faithfully. Falling counts with rising anti-dsDNA and low complement require escalation, because marrow suppression alone rarely explains the pattern.

steps.say: Eye lesions are the mirror of brain and systemic microvascular disease. Cotton-wool spots with haemorrhages indicate active vasculitis. Dry eye and episcleritis are the benign end. New retinal spots require systemic escalation.
steps.tx: Eyes in lupus span trivial dryness to sight threatening vasculitis: dry eye **keratoconjunctivitis sicca** with episcleritis at one end, retinal **vasculitis** with **cotton-wool spots** (fluffy white axoplasmic lumps) and bleeds at the other. Spots on the retina mirror inflamed vessels in brain and body. Fresh spots trigger systemic escalation, while lone dryness takes lubricants alone.

vis.alt: Butterfly facial rash of systemic lupus sparing the nasolabial folds.
vis.caption: The butterfly rash spares the nasolabial folds while retinal spots mark internal activity. Skin and retina are examined together. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Flares in one organ predict flares in others through shared complexes. Heart, lung, bowel, blood, and retina are reviewed at every active visit. Serology with complements guides the intensity. Remission in all five is the target.
steps.tx: Organ flares share immune complex pathogenesis, so active disease in one territory predicts others. Pericarditis at **25 to 50 percent**, haemorrhage with falling hematocrit, enteritis with comb sign, lymphopenia below **1,000**, and cotton-wool spots are each reviewed at every active visit. Rising anti-dsDNA with falling complements indicates escalation across all five territories together.

steps.say: Lupus is never a skin and joint disease alone in the exam. Pericardial rubs, falling counts, abdominal pain, breathlessness, and retinal spots are all scored. Each signature has its own therapy. The multisystem review is never skipped.
steps.tx: Lupus is never skin and joints alone: pericardial rubs, Libman-Sacks murmurs, infarctions above **50-fold** in young women, haemorrhage, enteritis, cytopenias below **1,000** lymphocytes, and cotton-wool spots complete the paper. Each signature carries its own therapy from pulse steroids to plasma exchange. The multisystem review at every visit is never skipped.

steps.say: Myocarditis hides behind unexplained tachycardia with troponin leak and new conduction defects. Coronaries are clean while biopsy shows immune complexes. Pulmonary hypertension is usually secondary to lung, clot, or left heart disease. Isolated vasculopathic hypertension needs catheter proof.
steps.tx: Unexplained fast pulse with **troponin** (heart injury protein) leak and fresh conduction blocks marks lupus **myocarditis** (inflamed heart muscle): coronaries run clean while biopsy carries immune complexes. Raised lung pressures in SLE are usually borrowed from interstitial disease, old clots, or left heart failure. True isolated vasculopathic hypertension is rare and earns targeted drugs only after right heart catheter proof.
